extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent prosecution practitioners (attorneys and agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for deciding whether and how to file a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) after a Final Office Action, including filing requirements, strategic alternatives, and cost considerations. Intended to help practitioners choose between RCE, appeal, continuation, and other after-final options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt of a Final Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE is appropriate when the applicant has received a Final Office Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of a Final Office Action is a primary trigger for considering an RCE because prosecution on the merits has been closed. Use this as a starting condition when evaluating post-final options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire to make further claim amendments or arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: File an RCE if the applicant wishes to make additional claim amendments and/or present further arguments to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE reopens prosecution and permits more substantial amendments than after-final practice; ensure proposed amendments are substantive and responsive to examination grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of new evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE is appropriate when new evidence that bears on patentability has become available since the Final Office Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New evidence (e.g., experimental data, declarations) can justify reopening prosecution. Evaluate whether the evidence materially affects allowed subject matter or examiner's basis for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for further dialogue to lead to allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider an RCE if continued engagement with the examiner could reasonably result in allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the examiner's responsiveness and whether prior arguments/amendments were close to persuasive. If meaningful back-and-forth remains possible, an RCE may be worthwhile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to consider new prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an RCE when new prior art needs to be addressed or incorporated into prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new cited references require claim changes or new arguments to overcome rejections, an RCE allows formal presentation and amendment to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must file before abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE must be filed before the application becomes abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is absolute: do not allow the application to lapse. Monitor abandonment dates and file the RCE in time to preserve the application and priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: File generally before the reply period for a Final Office Action expires
rubrics_metrics.description: RCEs are generally filed before the reply period for a Final Office Action expires (3 months ordinarily, extendable to 6 months with fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan filings around statutory/reply deadlines. If seeking extensions, include required extension fees and be aware of timing for preservation of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE must include an amendment, argument, or other response
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE needs to include an amendment, substantive argument, or other responsive material rather than being merely procedural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the RCE submission contains substantive content addressing the Final Office Action; merely filing to buy time without new substance is improper and may be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit an RCE without a substantive reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting an RCE without a substantive reply is an anti-pattern and may result in dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using RCEs as placeholders. The office expects meaningful amendments or arguments — otherwise the RCE risks being dismissed and fees wasted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on multiple RCEs — consider appeal after repeated RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more RCEs have already been filed, further RCEs may be unproductive; consider a patent appeal instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple RCEs often indicate fundamental disagreement with the examiner. Evaluate whether further RCEs will change the outcome or just increase cost and delay; appeals may be more effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFCP 2.0 (After Final Consideration Pilot) as an alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: AFCP 2.0 is an after-final pilot allowing free, limited amendments as an alternative to an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AFCP 2.0 when eligible to pursue limited amendments at no additional filing fee; suitable for narrow, targeted changes rather than broad prosecution reopening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Conference Request as an alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pre-Appeal Brief Conference Request offers a 5-page summary review by three examiners as an alternative to filing an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider this when there are clear legal or factual errors that can be summarized succinctly; it is a lower-cost way to seek reconsideration before appeal or RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal and Appeal Brief (PTAB) as an alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a Notice of Appeal and Appeal Brief brings the matter to the PTAB for review instead of reopening prosecution via RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appeal when the examiner's rejections raise issues suitable for judicial/administrative review; appeals can bypass repeated examiner dialogue but may be more time-consuming and costly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation application as an alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a continuation application creates a new application with potentially new claims and a new examination instead of an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider continuation when you want to pursue different claim scope or strategies while preserving the parent priority date; continuations involve fresh examination and can be strategic for claim portfolio management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost: escalating fees for subsequent RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: First RCE has a lower fee; second and subsequent RCEs carry higher fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor increasing PTO fees into the decision to file multiple RCEs. Higher fees for repeat RCEs are a fiscal signal to assess alternative paths like appeal or continuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost: each RCE delays patent issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each RCE delays the eventual issuance of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider downstream commercial and enforcement effects of delayed issuance (e.g., market timing, licensing). Delay can be an indirect cost of choosing continued prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple RCEs may indicate fundamental disagreement with the examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing many RCEs is an indicator that the applicant and examiner fundamentally disagree over patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a diagnostic: persistent disagreement suggests pausing to consider appeal or different claim strategy rather than repeating RCE filings that are unlikely to resolve the dispute.
